summary: Request backport: fix KV cache compaction crash to Runtime 1.18 LTS line
description:
Customer (Helio Health) is piloting Runtime 1.18 LTS candidate for Redwood Private. They are seeing a hard crash in the serving runtime under sustained traffic that appears correlated with KV cache compaction.

Issue summary
- Symptom: runtime process exits (SIGSEGV) during KV cache compaction; Kubernetes restarts the pod.
- Customer-observed impact: intermittent 5xx spikes during pod restart window; degraded throughput for ~2–4 minutes while HPA replaces capacity.
- Frequency: ~3–6 crashes/day across a 6-pod runtime pool (A100 80GB).
- Request: backport the known fix for KV cache compaction crash into the Runtime 1.18 LTS patch line ASAP; customer wants a pinned artifact + checksum they can roll out during their next maintenance window.

Severity assessment (Support)
- Severity: Sev1 / Priority P0
- Rationale: production crash with customer-facing errors; regulated healthcare workload; they require a stable LTS baseline and are blocked from expanding rollout until fixed.

Environment
- Deployment: Redwood Private (customer-managed EKS)
- Runtime version: 1.18.0-lts-rc2 (customer label; built from runtime-1.18-lts branch at time of pilot)
- GPUs: A100 80GB (6 pods; 1 GPU per pod)
- Traffic pattern: mixed prompt lengths; long-lived chat sessions; streaming enabled; tool/function calling disabled
- Config notes:
  - prefix caching enabled
  - kv_cache_compaction enabled (default)
  - max_sequence_length = 8192

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided)
1) Run sustained load with mixed prompt lengths (256–6k tokens) and keep ~30–60 concurrent chat sessions open for >20 minutes.
2) Enable streaming and send periodic follow-ups that extend context near max_sequence_length.
3) After 15–45 minutes, one pod crashes during a compaction cycle; crash rate increases when concurrent sessions are higher.

Expected result
- No runtime crash; requests should either complete or fail gracefully.

Actual result
- Runtime exits; in-flight requests return 500/connection reset; pod restarts.

Artifacts / logs (redacted)
- Customer log excerpt:
  - "FATAL kv_cache: compaction failed: invalid span length" 
  - "signal: segmentation fault (core dumped)"
- Stack trace top frames (customer redacted file names/paths):
  - kv_cache::compaction::move_blocks()
  - kv_cache::compaction::run_compaction()
  - scheduler::tick()

Customer request / acceptance criteria
- Provide an LTS patch (or RC) with the fix included, signed + checksums.
- Confirm perf gates passed (no >2% p95 regression on canonical workloads).
- Provide a short upgrade/rollback note for Private deployments.

Internal notes
- Likely matches known issue discussed in #eng-runtime (KV cache compaction crash repro thread).
- Fix believed to already exist on mainline; needs backport to runtime-1.18-lts with minimal diff.

Backport tracking (Support-facing)
- Target branch: runtime-1.18-lts
- Target patch: 1.18.1-lts (or 1.18.0-lts-p1 depending on release naming)
- Owner(s): Runtime (Samir Qureshi / Noah Patel), Release Eng (Connor O'Brien)
- Required gates: release branch CI + scheduler regression suite + perf-canary LTS gate

Workaround (temporary)
- If needed before patch is available: disable KV cache compaction (kv_cache_compaction=false) and scale pods + increase GPU headroom. Customer notes this increases memory pressure and may reduce throughput; acceptable only as a short-term mitigation.

Customer validated in staging and rolled to prod; crash no longer reproducible under sustained load. Temporary workaround (disable kv_cache_compaction) was provided but not required after patch.
